diagnosis: I calibrated the model with DDS against daily NSE over 1971-10 to 1997-12, after a one-year warm-up. I set the starting soil and groundwater stores close to their long-run levels so the run does not drift at the start. The full period gives NSE 0.863, KGE 0.92, bias +1.8% and r 0.94. The 1986-1997 part on its own gives NSE 0.877 and bias -0.6%. That part was not held out, since it is inside the calibration window, but it shows no drift between periods. The Thet responds slowly, with a low runoff ratio and a smooth hydrograph. The model reproduces this with a large soil store (FC about 390 mm, LP 0.70, BETA 3.1), which explains the strong evaporation losses. It also uses a groundwater recession of about 23 days (K2 0.043), PERC 1.5 and smoothing over about 4 days (MAXBAS 4.3). Snow matters little. The main weaknesses are probably the multi-year swings in chalk and sand groundwater, such as the drought years and wet winters, and the timing of the first wet-up in autumn. A single linear groundwater store cannot fully capture those slow changes. A second independent calibration found a different parameter set with a lower NSE (0.839), so several parameter combinations fit almost as well. I am fairly confident in the water balance and the overall dynamics. I am less confident in the individual response parameters (K0, UZL) and the snow parameters, which are poorly constrained.
